Chain rule for functions of two variables

Sacrificial anodic and impressed-current cathodic protection

topics: Nanomaterial classification by dimension and material
Carbon nanotubes, fullerenes, graphene and carbon quantum dots

modules.title: Molecular spectroscopy and analytical techniques
topics: Types of spectra and molecular energy levels
Vibrational modes of CO2 and H2O

modules.title: Environmental chemistry
topics: Primary, secondary and tertiary sewage treatment

courses.title: Engineering Graphics and Computer Aided Drawing

topics: Technical drawing relevance, line types, dimensioning and BIS conventions
Projection of points in different quadrants
Straight lines inclined to one or both planes

topics: Triangular, rectangular, square, pentagonal and hexagonal prisms and pyramids
Axes inclined to one reference plane
Axes inclined to both reference planes

Dimensioned two-dimensional drawings with suitable software

courses.title: Introduction to Electrical and Electronics Engineering
notes: One assessed course in the supplied syllabus. Keep Electrical and Electronics as separate teacher notebooks linked to this shared course. Modules 1-2 and 3-4 provide the initial electrical/electronics mapping; teacher coverage still needs confirmation.

modules.title: DC circuits and magnetic circuits
topics: Capacitor and inductor V-I relations and stored energy
Ohm and Kirchhoff laws with numericals
MMF, field strength, flux density and reluctance
Comparison of electrical and magnetic circuits
Series and parallel magnetic circuits with composite materials
notes: Star-delta derivation is not required.
Magnetic-circuit numerical problems are not required.

modules.title: Electromagnetic induction and AC circuits
topics: Self and mutual inductance and coefficient of coupling
Pure R, L and C circuits
Balanced star and delta connections and line/phase relations
notes: Induction/inductance numericals are marked not required.
AC waveform, impedance and three-phase sections include numerical problems.

modules.title: Electronic devices and circuits
topics: Ripple factor with and without capacitor filters
CE input/output characteristics and comparison of CE/CB/CC

modules.title: Communication, instrumentation and electronics applications
topics: IoT smart-home, healthcare and agriculture case studies
notes: AM/FM derivations are not required.
IoT applications are case studies only.

courses.title: Algorithmic Thinking with Python
notes: The header calls this Theory, but teaching hours, internal assessment and later pages explicitly include programming/lab components. Preserve both rather than discarding the practical work.
Includes 12 sample classroom exercises and 18 lab exercise entries, not the student's current assignment sheet or exam portion.

Source exercise 6 prints an ambiguous temperature-conversion expression; authored teaching material must use C/5=(F-32)/9. The collinearity exercise also needs vertical-line-safe handling. Do not silently treat source wording as verified worked solutions.

modules.title: Problem solving and Python essentials
topics: Computer as a model of computation
Algorithm development, programming, testing and evaluation

modules.title: Pseudocode and flowcharts
topics: Repetition with for, while and repeat-until
notes: Flowcharts are for visualizing control flow; RAPTOR is suggested.
Sample problems include arithmetic expressions, simple interest, comparisons, grade selection, descending sequences, sums, factorial and largest values.

modules.title: Python control flow, sequences, functions and recursion
topics: Lists, tuples, sets, strings and dictionaries
Recursive Fibonacci, GCD, factorial, addition and digit sums
notes: Merge sort and returning the top three integers are named decomposition/modularization examples.

modules.title: Computational problem-solving approaches
topics: Divide and conquer with merge sort
Greedy characteristics and comparison with dynamic programming
notes: Introductory diagrammatic/algorithmic explanations only; analysis is not required.

courses.title: Basic Electrical and Electronics Engineering Workshop
notes: Separate practical course. ESE is conducted internally; do not treat it as the same written exam as the theory course.
Eight electrical and nine electronics experiment entries. Minimum seven experiments from each specialization; actual class selection and completion are unknown.

Certified laboratory record is a submission prerequisite for the examination. The detailed continuous-assessment discussion does not visibly allocate all 45 continuous-assessment marks; preserve the top-level table and flag local rubric details for teacher confirmation.
